scenario: NVDA trades at $148.20, up 38% over the last six months. The 50-day MA ($138) is above the 200-day MA ($121), both sloping up. Higher highs and higher lows for nine consecutive weeks. Today's close prints a fresh 52-week high on volume 22% above the 20-day average. The Aggressive Debator is asked whether this is an entry.
question: What is the Aggressive Debator most likely to say?
options: Short it — extended moves always mean-revert
Enter long — every trend-following box is ticked: 50>200 MA both rising, nine-week sequence of HH/HL, 52-week high on above-average volume
Skip — NVDA is up 38% so the move is over
Wait for a 20% pullback before entering
explanation: Trend-following demands three things: a defined trend (50-day above 200-day, both rising), price structure confirming it (nine weeks of higher highs and higher lows), and a trigger (fresh 52-week high on above-average volume). NVDA prints all three. The Aggressive Debator's job is to push for the entry when the conditions align. The tempting wrong answer ('it's up 38% so the move is over') is the classic mean-reversion bias applied to a trending stock — trend-following explicitly buys strength, it doesn't fade it.

scenario: KLCI has oscillated between 1,540 and 1,605 for the last 11 weeks. The 50-day MA sits at 1,572 and is flat. Realised 30-day volatility is 8.4% annualised, near a two-year low. Bear market — low volume means distribution is happening
Bull market — flat MA and low volatility mean buyers are in control
Sideways / range-bound regime — flat 50-day MA, contained 65-point range, low vol, no sector leadership, breadth at neutral 51%
explanation: Five signals all say range-bound: a flat 50-day MA, 11 weeks inside a defined band (1,540–1,605), realised vol near two-year lows, sub-average volume, and breadth at the 50% neutral line with no sector leadership. That is the textbook sideways regime. The tempting wrong answer 'bull market' fails because a bull regime requires a rising MA and breadth above 60% — flat and 51% is the opposite signal. Low vol is not high vol; 'indecision' is the definition of sideways, not volatility.

explanation: Mean reversion assumes price oscillates around a stable mean. In a confirmed downtrend (200-day sloping down, death cross, six lower lows) the 'mean' is itself falling — every oversold bounce is a sell, not a buy. The user's own mandate codifies this: mean reversion only when the 200-day is flat or rising. XOM fails that test. The tempting wrong answer 'no stop attached' fails because nothing in the scenario claims the order is unprotected — the violation is upstream: the strategy doesn't belong in this regime at all.

The tempting wrong answer 'buy half on a pullback to $215' fails because $215 is below the range floor — if price returns there the breakout is invalidated, you don't add to a failed trade.

scenario: VIX spot is 34.8, up from 14.2 four weeks ago. The VIX 20-day average is 26. SPX 30-day realised vol has risen from 11% to 23%. Daily SPX moves have averaged 1.6% absolute over the last 10 sessions vs a year-to-date average of 0.7%. Put/call ratio is at a 12-month high of 1.42.

The tempting wrong answer 'bull market — VIX is contrarian' is dangerous half-knowledge: VIX spikes can mark bottoms, but only after they peak and roll over. Calling the regime bullish while it is still climbing is front-running mean reversion in the wrong tape.

scenario: User runs a trend-following system that worked great in 2023–2025. In 2026 H1 the system has had 11 trades, 9 of them stopped out at the same -3% loss, all 9 inside the same 14-week SPX range between 4,200 and 4,380. KLCI is similarly range-bound. VIX averaged 13 over the period. The user asks the Conservative Debator to diagnose the drawdown.
question: What is the Conservative Debator most likely to say?
options: Strategy failure mode — trend-following is regime-dependent and the current SPX/KLCI regime is sideways with low vol; the system isn't broken, it's running in the wrong regime, and should be paused or switched to a range/mean-reversion variant
Add more leverage to recover faster
The system is broken — abandon trend-following forever
explanation: EDGE 14 names this exactly: every strategy has a regime where it underperforms, and trend-following's failure regime is sideways/low-vol. The 9-for-11 stop-out pattern, all inside a defined SPX range, is the diagnostic fingerprint. The Conservative Debator's call is to recognise the regime, pause the system, and switch to a regime-appropriate tactic — not to abandon the edge. The tempting wrong answer 'abandon trend-following forever' is the emotional response to drawdown; the analyst response is to identify the regime mismatch and adapt.
